On a bounded interval with Neumann boundary conditions, we construct smooth, time-independent transmission and recovery rates satisfying \(β(x)>γ(x)>0\), together with diffusion coefficients \(d_I>d_S>0\), such that periodic solutions coexist with the unique endemic equilibrium for every prescribed positive total population. Thus, pointwise dominance of transmission over recovery does not ensure convergence to equilibrium. Our approach combines an inverse construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium with a coefficient path that preserves both the equilibrium and the pointwise inequalities. A change in the number of unstable eigenvalues along this path yields small-amplitude periodic solutions through a center-manifold reduction and a generalized Hopf bifurcation argument. The proof uses an AI-assisted construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium under the pointwise condition $β>γ>0$.

title: Affine $G$-multibiquandle modules for colored links I: representability of coloring functors and color-profile polynomials
abstract:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $G$ be an abelian group, and fix $u\in R[G]^\times$. For each component-labeled oriented link diagram $(D,σ)$, we construct a finitely presented $R[G]$-module $M_u(D,σ;R[G])$ with a universal affine coloring $U_{D,σ}$. Every affine coloring with values in an $R[G]$-module factors uniquely through $U_{D,σ}$ by a module homomorphism. Thus the module represents the affine coloring functor. Each specified colored Reidemeister move induces a unique module isomorphism compatible with coloring transport, and the module isomorphism class is a colored-link invariant. The representing modules and universal colorings commute with arbitrary scalar extension, without a flatness assumption. For classical links, simultaneous rescaling of the component labels removes the common deformation unit.
  For any multibiquandle, associated-biquandle colorings decompose into fibers indexed by component labelings. For finite targets and palettes, we define a color-profile polynomial recording the joint distribution of fiber sizes and numbers of palette labels used, and prove its invariance under oriented link isotopy. In the affine case, the representing modules determine these fibers, and their specialized dimensions determine the coloring counts over finite fields. The color-profile polynomial is not determined, in general, by the full unweighted distribution of coloring-fiber sizes. It therefore retains information beyond the associated-biquandle coloring count.

title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
abstract: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2πi}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2π(k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).

title: Calibrations close to $\mathrm{G}_2$-twistor space
abstract: We study natural structures of the kind of $\mathrm{G}_2$ existing on the unit tangent sphere bundle $SM \rightarrow M$ of any oriented Riemannian 4-manifold $M$. Based on the Harvey-Morgan classification of degree 3 calibrations on $\mathbb{R}^7$, we identity those which can be found on $SM$. We also study the Laplacian of the Sasaki metric on 3-forms.

title: From Common Information to Canonical Correlation Analysis and Beyond: Bridging Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning
abstract: Many problems in signal processing, machine learning, and neuroimaging provide several jointly observed measurements of one process, each mixing a component common to all of them with a component private to itself, and require the common component to be recovered without supervision. This problem has been studied in several communities, largely independently. Statisticians proposed canonical correlation analysis (CCA), introduced by Hotelling in 1936. Information theorists proposed two notions of common information, due to Gács and Körner and to Wyner. Engineers developed subspace methods for sensor arrays and multiuser communications to design multiview receivers. This tutorial presents the main results and tools each community developed for this problem in a single exposition, and explains the connections that emerge where they meet, distinguishing exact equivalences from special cases and analogies. We develop the information-theoretic foundation from first principles. We then introduce CCA and its extension to several views, followed by the engineering thread from blind multiuser detection to CCA as a blind receiver. Next, we turn to nonlinear CCA, covering kernel, deep, and probabilistic formulations, the conditions under which the common factor is identifiable, and connections to self-supervised learning. We conclude with a discussion of further extensions and open directions. The exposition is self-contained, so that readers from each of these communities can follow the parts developed by the others.

title: On the automorphisms of Pick bodies
abstract: We determine the biholomorphic automorphisms of the Pick body associated with finitely many distinct points in a Carathéodory hyperbolic domain. Every automorphism is the composition of a common disc automorphism applied to all coordinates and a coordinate permutation preserving the Pick body. The proof uses the quotient Banach algebra of interpolation data, its generalized von Neumann inequality, and the fact that its symmetric part consists precisely of the constant vectors. For nodes in a polydisc, we introduce minimal effective coordinate tuples and identify the admissible permutations with the automorphisms of a lower-dimensional polydisc that preserve the projected node set. This yields a direct-product description of the automorphism group, with one factor equal to the automorphism group of the disc and the other finite. We also give the resulting descriptions for nodes in the disc and the bidisc.

title: Self-Supervised Tuning of Low-Fidelity Optimization Models via High-Fidelity Feedback
abstract: Low-fidelity (LF) optimization models are widely used in large-scale operations because they can be solved efficiently and reliably, but they often exhibit systematic errors relative to high-fidelity (HF) formulations that better capture physical and operational constraints. Existing learning-based approaches typically rely on supervised or semi-supervised training with HF solutions, which are expensive to compute and may not align with HF operational objectives. We propose a self-supervised framework that parameterizes LF optimization models directly from HF feedback. The low-fidelity problem is embedded as a differentiable optimization layer and trained end-to-end, while a HF correction problem evaluates its solution and provides gradient information through its dual variables, without requiring HF solution labels. We evaluate the framework on optimal power flow, optimal gas flow, and pooling problems, spanning different sources of low- and high-fidelity mismatch. Across all three applications, the self-supervised approach improves objective quality and feasibility over untuned LF models and generally outperforms semi-supervised training. The learned parameterizations also generalize to unseen operating conditions and, for network applications with up to 30,000 nodes, to systems not encountered during training.

title: A Matroidal Framework for Random Access in Linear Codes
abstract: We study random access in linear codes when codeword symbols are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement. A code is recovery balanced if the expected number of samples required to recover a codeword coordinate is the same for every coordinate. We express the recovery expectations in terms of the associated matroid and derive a coordinatewise identity relating these values for a code and its dual. This proves that a linear code is recovery balanced if and only if its dual is recovery balanced, establishing a conjecture of Gruica et al. We further define the recovery balance for arbitrary matroids and show that asymptotically almost every sparse paving matroid is not recovery balanced.

title: Low-degree filtrations in ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology
abstract:
We prove the Hilbert-series formulas conjectured by Reiner--Tudose and by the Polymath Jr. Grassmannian group for the subalgebras of ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology generated in bounded degree. We determine the finite coefficient images underlying the proofs, together with the kernels of the coefficient and cancellation maps. We also construct bases adapted to the auxiliary ideal filtrations and identify the cancellation layers, as modules, with shifts of finite complete-intersection algebras. First-order deformations give the derivative inclusions needed to recover the filtration increments.
  We disprove the two ordinary basis conjectures of the Polymath group. For every $r\ge 2$, the span of each prescribed family has codimension one in weight $3r+2$ of $H^{2*}(\operatorname{Gr}(2,3r+1);\mathbb Q)$; replacing one index gives a basis in each of these components. More generally, each prescribed two-row family has codimension at most one in every weight. Weights are half the cohomological degrees, and all coefficients are rational.

title: Outer automorphisms of HNN extensions of abelian groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a commensurating HNN extension of a finitely generated free abelian group. We characterise when $\mathrm{Out}(G)$ is finitely generated and derive structural information about the group. We give soluble and non-soluble examples of commensurating HNN extensions of finitely generated free abelian groups with outer automorphism group not finitely generated.

title: Approximating the Ellipse Perimeter by "Bending the Line": The ELIP Closed-Form Family
abstract:
The perimeter of an ellipse is expressed exactly through the complete elliptic integral of the second kind, motivating accurate closed-form approximations. We introduce ELIP (Ellipse Linear Interpolated Perimeter), a family built by correcting the straight line joining the two exact normalized endpoint values. Two branches are developed: logarithmic-power corrections with optional deformation and exponential modulators, and rational-logarithmic corrections incorporating the exact asymptotic behavior of highly elongated ellipses. The framework distinguishes coefficients fixed analytically by Maclaurin matching from parameters optimized numerically by minimax fitting.
  Compact rationalized formulas achieve maximum relative errors of approximately 6.84, 3.57, 0.904, and 1.596 ppm. An ELIP R5,2 + 3 log formula with three fitted degrees of freedom has a certified maximum relative error below 0.001623 ppm. For ELIP R5,3 + 3 log, all rational-core coefficients are determined by exact Maclaurin matching. A one-parameter multiplicative correction, 1 - A*h^12*(1-h)^(7/4), reduces the certified global error bound to below 0.000452 ppm. This formula matches the exact perimeter series through h^8, while the correction starts at order h^12. The results provide a systematic approach combining exact endpoint geometry, local series constraints, elongated-limit logarithmic asymptotics, and low-dimensional numerical optimization.

title: Near-Horizon Scalar-Wave Sampling: Rindler Bounds and Schwarzschild Comparison
abstract: We study classical reconstruction of an outgoing scalar-wave component from radial-shell observations. Starting from the noncompact-time Rindler metric, we construct Klein--Gordon evolution by closed quadratic forms and reduce the massless characteristic dynamics to translation in optical distance. For an initial optical interval of length $L$, a shell of width $d$, and recording time $T$, the optimal squared observability bounds are $A(T,L)=\min\{d,(T-L)_+\}$ and $B(T,L)=\min\{d,T\}$. At $T=L$, the Rindler observation map is injective with nonclosed range. Discrete shell observations form a spatial fusion frame precisely when their transported regions cover the initial interval; we compute optimal uniform-grid bounds and characterize robustness under profile erasures. Finite-resolution reconstruction separates localization error, approximation error and noise amplification. For fixed Schwarzschild mass and angular momentum, we compare the scalar-wave observation operator with its Rindler limit. Anchored finite-energy preparation permits arbitrary prescribed outgoing $L^2([-L,0])$ profiles without a zero-integral condition. The operator error is explicitly $O(e^{-2κa})$ as an apparatus of fixed optical size is translated toward the horizon; whenever $T>L$, positive Rindler bounds transfer to Schwarzschild for all sufficiently large $a$. A positive Schwarzschild lower bound is impossible at or below the optical travel time, for every translation. These results concern classical observation and reconstruction, not quantum information or dissipative horizon evolution.

title: On Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds
abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of non-flat Lorentzian manifolds, called Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds (briefly, LTFSMs). This class contains Lorentzian concircular structure manifolds (briefly, LCSMs), LSP-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds with coefficient $α$, LP-$α$-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds, and LP-$α$-Kenmotsu manifolds. The interrelations among these various classes of manifolds are illustrated in Figures 1 and 2. We investigate several geometric properties of LTFSMs. In particular, we show that the expansion scalar, given by the divergence of $ξ$, is nonzero and nonconstant, and that the flow of $ξ$ is irrotational. In an LCSM, the Ricci operator commutes with the structure tensor $φ$ [12]. However, it is shown that, in an LTFSM, the Ricci operator does not generally commute with $φ$. If the gradient of the torse-forming scalar $α$ is collinear with the torse-forming vector field $ξ$, then the Ricci operator commutes with $φ$, and the manifold reduces to an LCSM. It is known that a conformally flat LCSM is quasi-Einstein and hence is a manifold of quasi-constant curvature. We show that a conformally flat LTFSM is a generalized quasi-Einstein manifold in the sense of Chaki [1] and is also a manifold of generalized quasi-constant curvature. Several curvature-related properties of LTFSMs are established, and their sectional curvature is determined. The existence of LTFSMs is demonstrated through several proper nontrivial examples. We also present examples that are simultaneously LCSMs and LTFSMs, examples of LTFMs characterizing twisted cubic spacetimes, and generalized Robertson-Walker (GRW) spacetimes characterizing LCSMs. Finally, we provide examples of LTFSMs in which the vector field $ξ$ is a unit timelike torse-forming vector field but is not concircular; see Examples 5.6--5.8.

title: Every tournament of dichromatic number $10 k^2$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood has dichromatic number more than $k$
abstract: The dichromatic number of a tournament is the minimum number of colors needed to color the vertices so that no directed cycle is monochromatic. Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour (2025) asked whether every tournament with dichromatic number $2k$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood induces a subtournament of dichromatic number at least $k$. We answer their question negatively by finding an example with dichromatic number $Ω(k^2)$. Furthermore, this quadratic bound is tight up to a constant factor; we show that for every integer $k \geq 1$, every tournament of dichromatic number $Ω(k^2)$ contains a vertex whose out-neighborhood induces a subtournament of dichromatic number more than $k$. This improves the previous best bound $\mathcal{O}(k^2\log k)$ due to Colinot and Newman (2026). To show this, we prove that every tournament of fractional dichromatic number $c$ has a dominating set of size at most $5c-1$. The proof uses Brouwer's fixed point theorem.

title: Tree-independence number VIII. 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number
abstract: A three-path-configuration is a graph consisting of three pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths, the union of every two of which is an induced cycle of length at least four. A graph is 3PC-free if no induced subgraph of it is a three-path-configuration. We show that 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number, which is asymptotically best possible.

title: Pappus configurations in the Hall plane
abstract: In this paper, we investigate Pappus configurations in the finite affine Hall plane. In particular, we show that for any two lines $\ell_1,\ell_2$ and for any triple of points on $\ell_1$ there is a triple of points on $\ell_2$ that are contained in a Pappus configuration, thus improving on the results of [F. Lazebnik and L. Leshock. On Pappus configurations in Hall planes. Des. Codes Cryptogr. 90 (2022), 1203--1219.].

title: A proof of Ward's conjecture on Griesmer codes
abstract: Let $C$ be an $[n,k,d]_q$ Griesmer code, where $q=p^f$ with $p$ prime, and write $e=ν_p(d)$. Ward conjectured that $C$ is $p^{\max\{0,e-f+1\}}$-divisible. In this paper, we prove this conjecture.

title: Day Convolution and Homotopy Groups on the Pointed Homotopy Category of CW Complexes
abstract: We freely enrich the pointed homotopy category of CW complexes over abelian groups and equip the resulting functor category with the enriched Day convolution induced by the smash product. After identifying the convolution unit and recording the coherence maps, we compute the convolution of the homotopy-group functors. For integers $n,m\geq 2$ we construct a natural isomorphism $π_n\starπ_m\congπ_{n+m}$ induced by the external smash product; equivalently, the external smash product is the universal natural pairing of homotopy groups. Under this identification, the symmetry interchanging the two factors acts on $π_{n+m}$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{nm}$.

title: Temporal-Logical Stochastic Processes
abstract: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for Temporal-Logical Stochastic Processes (TLSP), in which temporal-logic specifications induce time-indexed stochastic observables capturing the robustness of temporal satisfaction. Building upon existing probabilistic interpretations of temporal-logic robustness, we systematically investigate the stochastic-process structure of these observables. We establish their measurability, shifted-filtration adaptedness, and sample-path regularity under suitable assumptions, and characterize the action of temporal operators on stochastic processes. We derive pathwise perturbation bounds and quantify the sensitivity of temporal satisfaction probabilities through the probability mass concentrated near the logical boundary. A topology on the observable-process space and a semantic pseudometric on temporal formulas are introduced to establish convergence of temporal-logical observables under perturbations of formula parameters and temporal intervals. We further characterize conditions ensuring weak convergence of observable-process distributions and convergence of temporal satisfaction probabilities. Finally, we establish a process-level large-deviation principle for temporal-logical observables, providing a variational characterization of rare temporal events through minimum-action trajectories. The resulting framework connects temporal-logic semantics with stochastic-process topology, stability, convergence, and rare-event asymptotics, providing a mathematical foundation for the analysis of temporally constrained stochastic systems.

title: On the existence of independent inner functions
abstract: The existence of independent inner functions is established: there exist inner functions $\varphi$ and $ψ$, both vanishing at the origin, such that $$ \frac{1}{2π}\int_0^{2π} \varphi^m(e^{iθ}) \overline{ψ^n(e^{iθ})}\,dθ= 0, \qquad m,n \geq 1. $$ In fact, both $\varphi$ and $ψ$ can be chosen to be Blaschke products. The proof proceeds by an iterative construction, which suggests a general approach to produce inner functions with a desired joint distribution.

title: Partial regularity of heat flow of fractional harmonic maps to spheres
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notation of stationary heat flow of $s$-harmonic maps from $\R^m$ into the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{\ell-1}\hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^\ell$, for $0<s<1$, framed through the parabolic version of Caffarelli-Silvestre's extension. We prove that any stationary heat flow of $s$-harmonic maps is smooth away from a closed set of vanishing $(m+2-2s)$-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. This extends to the fractional settings the partial regularity theorem on the heat flow of harmonic maps into spheres by Chen-Li-Lin and Feldman.

title: Normal approximation and self-normalized moderate deviations for the minimal random walk with random step sizes
abstract: We study the minimal random walk with independent positive random step sizes. By separating the movement count from the centered step-size noise, we obtain normal approximations and self-normalized Cramér-type moderate deviations under finite-moment assumptions. For the noise, conditioning on the movement count yields Kolmogorov, Wasserstein and Zolotarev bounds. A polynomial moderate-deviation range holds when a recalled stop can lead to movement. At the boundary where this probability is zero, we obtain a logarithmic range and construct a bounded nonsymmetric example excluding a general polynomial range. For the full position, a weighted martingale representation gives limit laws in the different regimes, nonuniform normal approximations and moment-distance bounds without logarithmic losses. Variance concentration also yields self-normalized moderate deviations in the diffusive and critical regimes.

title: Small covers and the Four Color Theorem
abstract: We give a combinatorial proof that every simple convex $3$-polytope admits a small cover without using the Four Color Theorem. We also prove that the assertion that every simple plane triangulation admits a mod~$2$ characteristic function with at most five values is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem.

title: Inhomogeneous random graphs: how heavy tails reshape connectivity
abstract: We study inhomogeneous random graphs on $n$ vertices with independent Pareto weights of parameter $α>0$ and connection probabilities $\min(\varepsilon_n W_iW_j, 1)$. Our main focus is the infinite-mean regime $0<α<1$. Under the scaling $n\varepsilon_n^α=λ$, with $λ>0$ fixed, the global architecture of the graph is entirely governed by the Poisson point process $Π$ of rescaled extreme weights. In particular, the size of the largest component, divided by $n$, converges to a non-degenerate random variable expressed as an explicit functional of $Π$. Through the point process $Π$, we also characterize the exact limiting connectivity probability, uncovering a non-sharp connectivity threshold. The second largest component and the diameter of the largest component are bounded with high probability. The distance between two uniformly chosen vertices in the largest component is at most three with high probability. We also prove convergence of the point process of rescaled degrees and identify the limiting distribution of the maximum degree. For completeness, we obtain expected degree asymptotics, typical degree limits and connectivity regimes for all $α>0$. Due to the failure of classical branching process approximations in the infinite-mean regime, our approach relies fundamentally on analyzing the extreme weight environment $Π$.

title: Continuity of Furstenberg entropy on Bowen Poisson bundles
abstract: We provide a sufficient criterion for continuity of the Furstenberg entropy of Bowen Poisson bundles, jointly in the random walk measure and the underlying invariant random subgroup. The criterion applies in particular for tree-like Poisson bundles of a free group and for intersectional invariant random subgroups on lamplighter groups. It also provides continuity of the boundary entropy spectrum of powers of prime measured groups.

title: Harnack-type inequalities for nonlocal parabolic equations in the upper fast-diffusion range
abstract: We study non-negative weak solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear nonlocal parabolic equations of the form $$ (u^q)_t+\mathcal Lu=0, $$ where $\mathcal L$ is a nonlocal $p$-Laplace-type operator with a symmetric measurable kernel. We consider the fast-diffusion range $1<p<q+1$ and establish Harnack-type estimates in the upper fast-diffusion regime $\widetilde p_c<p<q+1$, where $\widetilde p_c$ is a critical exponent determined by the interplay between the temporal nonlinearity and the nonlocal diffusion. In particular, the estimates apply to the nonlocal parabolic $p$-Laplace equation and the nonlocal porous medium equation.

title: A recovery based linear finite element method for the Monge--Ampère equation
abstract: In this paper, we study finite element approximations of a fourth-order perturbed semilinear partial differential equation that arises naturally in the computation of viscosity solutions to the fully nonlinear Monge--Ampère equation. We develop a novel recovery-based $C^0$ linear finite element method for discretizing this model problem. The key analytical tool is a Miranda--Talenti-type estimate for the recovery operator, which guides the formulation of the discrete scheme and guarantees its well-posedness. We rigorously establish convergence in the $H^2$ norm by employing a fixed-point argument. Furthermore, optimal $H^1$-error estimates are derived using a duality argument. Numerical experiments confirm the efficiency of the proposed method and validate the theoretical convergence results.

title: Finite-to-One Maps into Band-Limited Function Spaces and Cubical Shifts with a Hurewicz Bound
abstract: Let $(X,T)$ be a dynamical system with the marker property and finite mean dimension $m$. We prove that, for every integer $D>m$, there exists an equivariant continuous map $f:X\to([0,1]^D)^{\mathbb Z}$ whose fibers contain at most $\lfloor D/(D-m)\rfloor$ points; in particular, $f$ is an embedding when $D>2m$. This is the dynamical analogue of the fiber bound in Hurewicz's classical theorem (1933) for continuous maps into Euclidean cubes. For every real number $a>m$, we also construct an equivariant continuous map from $X$ into the closed unit ball of the real Bernstein space of bounded continuous functions on $\mathbb R$ whose Fourier transforms, understood in the sense of distributions, are supported in $[-a/2,a/2]$, with each fiber containing at most $\lfloor a/(a-m)\rfloor$ points. The proof adapts the signal-analysis method of Gutman--Qiao--Tsukamoto (2019) to the finite-to-one setting and simplifies its analytic and geometric ingredients for $\mathbb Z$-actions.

title: Frequency Structure of AMM Liquidity Pools: A Multiresolution Analysis of Regime Transitions
abstract: This study examines the temporal structure of liquidity pools in constant-product automated market makers. Using a sample of eighteen pools observed at a five-minute frequency over two years, it aims to identify the temporal scales at which interactions within the system occur and how these interactions reorganize in response to changes in the volatility regime. Methodologically, the study proposes a strictly causal Haar multiresolution analysis in which each variable is estimated using only the information available at the time of measurement. Within this decomposition, three dimensions are examined: the scale composition of the return-to-risk relationship, the frequency-band coupling between pool activity and price volatility, and the detection of regime transitions using a fluctuation-to-trend indicator. The results reveal a clear structural segmentation: pool variability is concentrated at fast scales, whereas the relationships among its series, signal persistence, and information on subsequent performance reside at slow scales. Aggregate measures do not distinguish this separation because they combine both components before they can be compared.

title: Computing Theta Characteristics and their Galois action on general curves of moderate genus
abstract: In this article, we present an algorithm that, given a smooth curve $X$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, returns an explicit arithmetic representation of both odd and even Theta Characteristics split by parity. It allows us to retrieve their Galois action and étale algebra. The output includes the Theta Hyperplanes of the Theta Characteristics when they are finite, their associated proof functions as well as the dictionary of their quadratic forms. The algorithm works in a rather large generality as it handles any one-equation (potentially singular) model of smooth curves. The most binding requirement remains the necessity for an explicit degree 1 rational divisor on the curve or more likely a rational point. We implemented the algorithm and give examples up to genus $5$.

title: A spinor-adapted geometric approach to nonlinear Dirac systems on the Schwarzschild black hole background
abstract:
Building on our previous work, we extend the spinor-adapted geometric method for nonlinear Dirac systems from small perturbations of Minkowski spacetime to the Schwarzschild background. As a linear foundation, we establish integrated local energy decay estimates and an \(r^p\)-weighted energy hierarchy for spinor fields, adapting the physical-space approach of Dafermos and Rodnianski to the Dirac setting.
  The main focus of the paper is nonlinear. We consider a semilinear tensorial wave--Dirac model motivated by the wave-gauge reduction of the Einstein--Dirac system and prove global small-data stability. A principal difficulty is the apparent loss of derivatives arising from the coupling between the first-order Dirac equation and the second-order tensorial wave equation. We overcome this difficulty through a spinor-adapted energy hierarchy that exploits the complementary roles of the Dirac-current energy and the spinorial wave energy. In particular, the nonlinear estimates are closed without requiring the top-order Dirac-current estimate.
  The nonlinear analysis demonstrates that the spinorial structures remain essential on the black-hole background. The combination of Dirac-current energy, spinorial wave energy, Kosmann Lie derivatives, and the Clifford-algebraic null structure enables us to close the nonlinear estimates without imposing an independent null condition on the tensorial wave equation. Thus, the nonlinear closure relies fundamentally on structures intrinsic to the Dirac equation.
  A second main result is the global small-data stability of the Maxwell--Dirac system in the Lorenz gauge on the Schwarzschild background, under a vanishing-charge assumption. This extends the nonlinear stability theory to a genuine gauge-coupled Dirac system and demonstrates the applicability of the spinor-adapted physical-space approach beyond the tensorial wave--Dirac model.

title: Frobenius forms and semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras
abstract: We determine the Nakayama automorphism of the canonical homogeneous Frobenius form on cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras. We give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on the dominant weight and the rank for semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras of types $A_e^{(1)}$, $C_e^{(1)}$, $A_{2e}^{(2)}$, $D_{e+1}^{(2)}$, $A_\infty$, $B_\infty$, and $C_\infty$. As an application, we prove that a cyclotomic Hecke--Clifford superalgebra is semisimple if and only if the corresponding Poincaré polynomial is nonzero.

title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
abstract: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections. We define sectional curvature and a curvature form on the algebraic exterior square, and demonstrate an obstruction to the usual Ricci trace construction: on $C^\infty(S^1,S^2)$, the relevant curvature endomorphism extends boundedly to the $L^2$ completion but is not trace class. We prove the second variation formula, identify the energy Hessian with the index form, and characterize its null space. Under additional hypotheses, we establish existence and uniqueness of Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data. Finally, non-positive sectional curvature excludes conjugate points, while a negative index direction obstructs length minimization.

title: The Logarithmic A-Discriminant
abstract: We extend the GKZ theory of discriminants to the setting of Euler integrals where both coefficients and exponents are variables. The integrand is the likelihood function of a toric model in algebraic statistics, whose number of critical points is the volume of the Newton polytope. Our logarithmic A-discriminant vanishes when two critical points come together. This discriminant is a hypersurface, parametrized by the logarithmic Horn uniformization. Hurwitz forms of toric varieties yield a degree formula, and a description of leading coefficients. We emphasize applications and computations.

title: Algorithm duality from resolvent Moreau identities
abstract: Duality is classically defined as a relationship between objective functions, one that breaks down beyond convexity. We show that a more fundamental duality persists between the resolvent operators used to solve associated problems. We establish a framework from which we obtain complete characterizations of the duality-like correspondences between proximal fixed-point iterations and their alternating minimization scheme counterparts. Namely, we show the known primal-dual relationships between forward--backward splitting and Tseng's alternating minimization algorithm, and between the Douglas-Rachford method and alternating direction method of multipliers, to hold generically and irrespective of problem assumptions. The approach considered herein avoids the machinery of convex analysis entirely, providing a definitive formulation of algorithmic dualities in maximal generality while greatly simplifying their proofs. In particular, assumptions such as monotonicity, weak monotonicity, Lipschitz continuity, and injectivity of linear operators are all shown to be unnecessary. In addition, we utilize our framework to reveal and analyze a novel primal-dual relationship between backward-backward splitting and a special instance of the alternating minimization algorithm. This illustrates how our duality framework provides a principled basis for primal-dual algorithm design and analysis in nonmonotone settings. Finally, our experiments show that our backward--backward splitting--based approach reliably outperforms the FISTA and SR3 algorithms for the LASSO problem.

title: The first $\ell^2$-Betti number, cost and rank gradient of few-relator random groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a random group in the few-relator model with $n\ge 2$ generators and $m\ge 1$ relators. We prove that asymptotically almost surely the first $\ell^2$-Betti number, the cost minus one, and the absolute rank gradient of $G$ are all equal to $\max\{n-m-1,0\}$. In particular, the equality $β_1^{(2)}(G)=0$ when $m\ge n-1$ answers positively a conjecture of Kielak, Kropholler and Wilkes [J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2022].

title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
abstract:
Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity.
  Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.

title: Time-Uniform Dependent Central Limit Theory
abstract: We establish a near-optimal almost sure invariance principle for nonstationary time series under the functional dependence measure (FDM) framework. This result yields a universal time-uniform dependent central limit theorem, which serves as the basis for anytime-valid inference. In particular, we instantiate the theorem through asymptotic confidence sequences (AsympCSs), time-uniform counterparts of asymptotic confidence intervals obtained via central limit theorems, extending those originally proposed in Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) to time series with serial dependence. We further refine their definition because, as we show, it can admit AsympCSs that fail to achieve the desired asymptotic time-uniform coverage for a broad class of data-generating processes, including independent and identically distributed cases. We address this issue by adding a simple eventual-inclusion condition, which in turn permits more flexible variance estimation, particularly useful in time-series settings. For feasible implementation of AsympCSs, we establish strong consistency of HAC variance estimators under the FDM framework, accommodating a wider range of commonly used bandwidth choices than existing results under mixing conditions. As illustrations, we construct AsympCSs for algorithms with Markovian structure and time-series-based causal estimands.

title: Support periods of polynomials and support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes over Galois rings
abstract:
Let \(A=\GR(p^e,r)\) have residue field \(\F_q\), and let \(λ\in A^\times\). We relate coefficient compression of monic divisors of \(X^N-λ\) to support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes. At a simple-root length, the support period of every nonconstant monic divisor is preserved at each coefficient precision and equals the order of the multiplicative stabilizer of its root set. For a cyclic Frobenius-orbit polynomial, the multiple equal-difference structure determines its support period, core degree, and least relative degree of an unramified extension over which all its basic-irreducible factors are binomials.
  Coordinate projections give every constacyclic code over a finite commutative ring a unique maximal interleaving into copies of one support-primitive code. At simple-root lengths over \(A\), the intrinsic period of a code is the greatest common divisor of the periods of its torsion codes. The decomposition yields distance and duality formulas and the arithmetic Singleton bound for free codes. At every length, a nonzero code over \(A\) has the same minimum Hamming distance as its highest torsion code, which gives a refined bound. At repeated-root lengths, identical torsion filtrations can occur with different intrinsic periods, while a class of nonzero codes obtained by substitution from simple-root generators retains the same core and minimum distance.
  Trace matrices recover the coefficients of basic-irreducible cores using unit pivots, and local Hensel corrections lift compressed factors directly. For \(X^n-1\) with \(p\nmid n\), lifting and output have quasi-linear bit cost in the compressed representation when the arithmetic data and residue factorizations are given.

title: Group Distributionally Robust Optimization over Decentralized Networks
abstract: We study group distributionally robust optimization (GDRO) over decentralized networks, where workers collaborate to learn robust models by minimizing the maximum local risk. Existing methods optimize only dual-regularized surrogates and establish guarantees for a globally averaged model that is not available to workers. In this paper, we directly optimize the original GDRO objective and establish guarantees for local models in semi-decentralized (SemiDec) and fully decentralized (Dec) settings. A key difficulty is that applying the primal-dual decomposition from centralized GDRO yields worker-dependent losses whose evaluation requires unavailable cross-worker information. To address this challenge, we develop a novel error decomposition that recasts decentralized GDRO as (i) a decentralized online convex optimization (D-OCO) problem and a prediction-with-expert-advice problem in SemiDec, and as (ii) two coupled D-OCO problems in Dec, with discrepancy terms capturing inconsistencies among local decisions. By isolating consensus errors in analysis, we develop modular frameworks that support different consensus routines. We then establish the \emph{first} per-worker convergence guarantees for optimizing the original GDRO objective over decentralized networks. Instantiations with accelerated gossip and Choco-gossip achieve an $O(\sqrt{(\log m)/T})$ convergence rate over $T$ update rounds, while experiments demonstrate improved worst-worker performance over baselines.

title: Higher-order convex orders under free multiplicative convolution
abstract: We prove that free multiplicative convolution with a probability measure on $[0,\infty)$ preserves the $k$-convex order for every integer $k\ge2$, assuming finite $(k-1)$st absolute moments for the two measures being compared and for the convolving measure. The compared measures may have arbitrary support in $\mathbb{R}$.

title: Sharp asymptotics for a free boundary touching a degenerate boundary: the perpetual Heston put
abstract: We study the exercise boundary of the perpetual American put in the Heston model near zero variance. There the pricing operator degenerates, and the exercise boundary, a free boundary in the stock--variance half-plane, touches the boundary of the half-plane. No Feller condition is imposed. The boundary is analytic at positive variance and extends as a regular $C^1$ curve tangent to the zero-variance axis. Its approach to the axis follows one of three laws, according to whether the Feller ratio $2κθ/σ^2$ is larger than, equal to, or smaller than one: a logarithmic correction to linear order, an exponential correction in the square root of the logarithm, or a fractional power. In the first two cases the leading coefficients are explicit and the tangent is not Hölder continuous at the axis. In the third case the exponent is selected by a possibly nonsymmetric stable operator on the axis, and the amplitude is finite and positive.

title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
abstract: Let $Λ\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det Γ\ge 1$ for all sublattices $Γ\subseteq Λ^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that $f$ is $α$-strongly log-concave, where $α= 2π/e$, and $X + Λ$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/Λ$. Moreover, we show that the existence of such a density $f$ characterizes the assumption on $Γ$ up to a constant. There are a few consequences of the above. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ μ(Λ, K) = \max_{x \in \mathbb{R}^n} \min_{λ\in Λ} \|x-λ\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}π} \cdot \mathbb{E}_G\, \|G\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,I)$. This implies an $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. Second, we establish as a consequence an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem with an explicit constant.

title: A hybridization-derived interior penalty Nitsche method for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion
abstract: We develop an interior penalty Nitsche finite element formulation for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion problems, which is derived from an interior-penalty stabilized Lagrange multiplier method. A distinctive feature of the derived method is that it simultaneously combines two popular stabilization strategies: (i) a boundary penalty mechanism similar to Nitsche's methods and (ii) an interior penalty mechanism as for Continuous Interior Penalty (CIP) methods. Furthermore, the normal component of the numerical flux is single-valued across the mesh skeleton and available in closed form. We establish the equivalence between the hybridized Lagrange multiplier formulation and its condensed Interior Penalty Nitsche (IPN) form, and we deliver the stability and convergence analysis of the latter. For sufficiently regular solutions, we establish energy-norm error estimates for the three symmetry variants. Under a piecewise elliptic regularity assumption on the adjoint problem, the $L^2$ estimate is optimal for the symmetric variant and exhibits a half-order loss for the incomplete and nonsymmetric variants; its constant may depend on the diffusion coefficients through the adjoint regularity constant. This single-valued numerical normal flux, available in closed form, provides a starting point for locally conservative $H(\mathrm{div})$-conforming flux reconstruction, left for future work. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings.

title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
abstract:
We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $θ(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field.
  Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture.
  We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

title: A New Modification of the Milstein Method and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
abstract: The article presents a new modification of the Milstein method for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the first author in 2006. The article also provides the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients.

title: A Shadow Sequence Technique for Last-Iterate Convergence Analysis of the Random Reshuffling Method: Relaxed Stepsize Conditions and Beyond
abstract: We prove two last-iterate convergence bounds of the random reshuffling (RR) method in the smooth general convex finite-sum optimization. In the proved results, the stepsize sequence $\{η_{k}\}_{k}$ of RR is an arbitrary positive non-increasing sequence with $η_{1}\lesssim 1/(\operatorname{polylog}(n)L)$, where $n$ is the number of components of the finite-sum objective and $L$ is the smoothness parameter. Specifically, a last-iterate convergence rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{\Vert x_{1}^{1}-x_{*}\Vert^2}{n\sum_{k=1}^{K}η_{k}}+σ_{*}^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{η_{k}^{2}}{\sum_{l=k}^{K}η_{l}}\right)$ of RR is proved, where $x_{*}$ is a solution of the optimization problem and $σ_{*}^{2}$ is the variance at the solution $x_{*}$. This rate is novel to the last-iterate of RR. Also, a last-iterate convergence rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{\Vert x_{1}^{1}-x_{*}\Vert^2}{n\sum_{k=1}^{K}η_{k}}+nσ_{*}^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{η_{k}^{3}}{\sum_{l=k}^{K}η_{l}} \right)$ of RR is proved. A similar rate exists in the literature, but only under a restrictive stepsize condition $η\lesssim 1/(n L)$ and does not allow varying stepsizes. At the heart of our proof for the latter rate is an auxiliary sequence named the shadow sequence, which has the same epoch endpoints with the iterate sequence generated by RR. The shadow sequence can be regarded as an iterate sequence generated by performing an inexact RR on an auxiliary interpolated problem or performing a novel variant of random reshuffled SVRG on the original problem. The shadow sequence technique sheds light on deeper understanding of RR and may be useful in the analysis of other shuffling methods.

title: A Link-Based Algorithm for Stochastic User Equilibrium with Bounded Choice and Local Detour Threshold
abstract: This study develops a novel solution method for stochastic user equilibrium (SUE) under the bounded choice model with local detour threshold (BCM-LDT SUE; Rasmussen et al., 2024), which restricts the choice set in line with observed route choice behavior. The model assigns zero probability to paths whose total cost exceeds a bound or whose local detour exceeds a threshold; thus, the path choice set varies with link costs. The proposed algorithm updates link flows while implicitly enumerating the path choice set via a depth-first search (DFS) pruned with the BCM-LDT bounds. This distinguishes it from the original algorithm, which updates path flows, and enables quasi-Newton-type acceleration. Since paths are never stored, the method can handle choice sets totaling on the order of $10^7$ paths. On a personal computer, it reached equilibrium in a few to about fifteen minutes, not only for the Anaheim network under the original settings but also for larger networks such as Winnipeg and Barcelona.

title: A Computer-Assisted Proof that R(5,10;5,8)=21 for the Generalized Threshold Ramsey Number
abstract: We prove that the generalized threshold Ramsey number R(5,10;5,8) equals 21. This number corresponds to the set Ramsey number r_5(10,8) introduced by Harborth. The proof is computer-assisted. We first enumerate all (4,6;5,8)-good and (5,10;4,4)-good graphs. Then we apply the lucky-vertex inequality derived from the McKay--Radziszowski edge identity to filter candidate pairs for a gluing search, and encode the remaining cases as SAT instances. The search yields exactly 17 non-isomorphic (5,10;5,8;20)-good graphs. Finally, we exclude all one-vertex extensions of these 17 graphs, which proves that no (5,10;5,8;21)-good graph exists.Additionally, we update the tabulation of small set Ramsey numbers r_5(m,n) for 1 <= m,n <= 10.

title: The Conjugacy Problem for Recursively Presented Virtually Soluble Groups of Finite Prüfer Rank
abstract: We solve a long-standing conjugacy problem for finitely presented soluble groups of finite Prüfer rank, recorded as Problem~9.52 in the Kourovka Notebook, in the stronger setting of recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble groups. Robinson proved that, in every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble minimax group, conjugacy to any fixed element is decidable, while explicitly lefting open whether the procedure could be made uniform in the target element. We establish this uniformity. More specifically, we prove that every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble group of finite Prüfer rank has decidable Conjugacy Problem.

title: Data-driven calibration of a two-dimensional traffic flow model: Dimension reduction and optimization strategies
abstract: We study the data-driven calibration of a two-dimensional first-order macroscopic traffic flow model, in which the movement along and across the road is described by a three-parameter flux model. The calibration is based on three real-world datasets, ranging from microscopic drone trajectories on German highways to aggregated urban sensor measurements. We recall the well-posedness of the underlying scalar conservation law and derive structural properties of the flux model. In particular, one parameter enters linearly and can be eliminated analytically, which reduces the non-linear least-squares problem from three to two dimensions. We solve the full and reduced calibration problem with two local optimization methods, Nelder-Mead and L-BFGS-B, and three global population-based methods Differential Evolution, Consensus-Based Optimization, and its deterministic variant Quasi-Monte Carlo consensus based optimization. In addition to accuracy and computational cost, we examine how sensitive the objective is to the parameters and how robust the algorithms are with respect to randomness and initialization. The reduced formulation is considerably cheaper and less sensitive to the choice of optimizer. The local methods are the most efficient when suitably initialized, whereas the global methods are more robust.

title: Cartan Subalgebras of Dimension Drop Interval Algebras and Their Inductive Limits
abstract: We describe the conjugacy of non-degenerate Cartan subalgebras of the dimension drop interval algebras $M_m(\widetilde{\mathbb I}_p)$ in terms of double cosets of permutation groups, and describe their spectra by finite bi-partite multigraphs. All Cartan subalgebras are non-degenerate precisely when the two parameters are coprime. We also give splitting interval examples with prescribed finite numbers of Cartan conjugacy classes. Passing to inductive limits, we construct a unital simple AD algebra $\mathcal{A}$ of real rank zero and stable rank one, with $K_0(\mathcal{A})\cong\mathbb Z[1/3]$ and $K_1(\mathcal{A})\cong\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. It contains infinitely many mutually isomorphic but pairwise nonconjugate $\mathrm{C}^*$-diagonals. Their spectra are all homeomorphic to the dense amalgam of circles, while orbit multiplicities in the Weyl groupoids distinguish their embeddings. The same AD algebra also contains infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic Cartan subalgebras.

title: Avoiding two cycles in Avoider--Enforcer games
abstract: We study the strict and monotone $(1:b)$ Avoider--Enforcer games on the edges of the complete graph $K_n$. We prove that, for integers $n\ge2$ and $b\ge6n$, Avoider can keep his graph a forest after every move, except possibly the last. Thus, his final graph contains at most one cycle. This answers Question~10 of Clemens, Ehrenmüller, Person, and Tran, which asks whether a bias linear in $n$ is sufficient.

title: Revisiting the infinite Galois correspondence via group representations
abstract: Inspired by Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem, we interpret the Galois correspondence as a special case of a simple general principle in harmonic analysis on profinite groups. This also gives a representation-theoretic characterisation of profinite groups.

title: An entropy proof of the commonality of apices of trees
abstract: A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-colouring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random colouring with an equal proportion of each colour. Grzesik, Lee, Lidický and Volec conjectured that every $k$-apex of any connected Sidorenko graph is common. Recently, Kr{á}l', Krnc and Lamaison proved that the $k$-apex of any tree is common for $k\leq 5$. In this paper, we extend their result by showing that for every positive integer $k$, the $k$-apex of any tree or any forest with average degree at least one is common. Our proof involves an application of the entropy method.

title: General function bases moment models for suspended sediment with vertical profile of concentration
abstract: We introduce a general hydrostatic shallow moment framework for suspended sediment transport with vertically varying horizontal velocity and concentration profiles. The formulation is constructed over arbitrary vertical functional bases that are numerically orthogonalised via the Gram-Schmidt algorithm. This approach allows the approximation spaces for the vertical profile to be adapted to the specific structure of each physical variable, where also the velocity and sediment concentration can be projected onto different functional spaces. To overcome the limitations due to the inherent oscillatory nature of global Legendre polynomials, we explore a specific continuous piecewise linear $\mathbb{P}_1$ finite-element basis. Furthermore, non-uniform vertical partitions are considered, enabling an enhanced representation of the vertical profiles in specific regions. Numerical experiments involving boundary layers and suspended sediment transport demonstrate that the proposed framework is accurate to reproduce the expected vertical profiles. The improvement is particularly significant for sediment concentration profiles with sharp vertical variations, where polynomial reconstructions exhibit pronounced oscillations leading to physically meaningless profiles, whereas the $\mathbb{P}_1$ bases produce a qualitatively accurate representation of the vertical profiles observed in the sedimentation processes.

title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes
abstract: For every prime power $q>19683$, we settle the Cheng--Murray deep-hole problem for full-length Reed--Solomon codes in every dimension $2\le k\le q-2$, with the characteristic-two cases stated explicitly. For odd $q$, the deep holes are precisely the words of degree $k$. For even $q$ and $k\ge3$, the same conclusion holds except for an additional family when $k=q-3$. In even characteristic and dimension two, every deep hole has a unique expression $a h(X)+bX+c$, where $a\ne0$ and $h$ is a normalized $o$-polynomial. The proof combines quadratic quotient algebras, graph-theoretic weighted independent-set inequalities, and planar arc completion. We also obtain normal rational curve rigidity in the corresponding nonexceptional dimensions, the projective Reed--Solomon covering radii, and distinct-coordinate solvability and remainder criteria.

title: Local Lyapunov Exponent-Guided Stochastic Midcourse Correction Design of Low-Energy Earth-Moon Transfers
abstract: Midcourse correction is essential for reliable cislunar transfer missions. For low-energy Earth-Moon transfers, strongly nonuniform error growth makes conventional correction strategies less effective. This paper proposes a stochastic midcourse correction design for low-energy Earth-Moon transfers based on local Lyapunov exponent (LLE). The local error-amplification characteristics of the nominal trajectory are first analyzed using an instantaneous LLE. The analysis shows that strong sensitivity is concentrated near periapsis, and that the LLE maxima coincide with regions of strong finite-time error growth. These maxima are therefore used to segment the trajectory and define the number of corrections. Based on this segmentation, a reduced parameterization is introduced to describe the correction epochs, while second-order state transition tensors (STTs) are employed for nonlinear correction targeting. The resulting timing variables are then optimized through a sample-average approximation of the chance-constrained stochastic problem. Paired Monte Carlo simulations show that, under the same mission-accuracy requirements, the proposed strategy greatly improves the reliability and robustness of trajectory recovery while requiring less correction cost than the classical Breakwell spacing-ratio strategy.

title: Precision Coexistence: Angular-Spectral Region Constrained Waveform Design for MIMO-ISAC
abstract: In this paper, we develop a dual-function waveform design framework for multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments. In such environments, the dual-function waveform must coexist with legacy systems, such as localized positioning sensors, maritime radar networks, and satellite communication links, that occupy specific frequency bands and angular sectors. To enable precision coexistence, we incorporate localized angular-spectral region constraints that suppress beamformed energy only within the angle-frequency regions occupied by each legacy system, while preserving the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) available outside those regions. The resulting waveform design problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem and solved using a low-complexity majorization--minimization alternating direction method of multipliers (MM--ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides precise legacy-system protection while maintaining robust radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.

title: An Arnold-Type Stability Analysis of Vortex Filaments
abstract: We establish nonlinear orbital stability of circular arcs with opening angle $θ\le π$ and closed circles under the Localized Induction Equation (LIE), with prescribed endpoint constraints for arcs. Our Arnold-type variational approach combines two conserved quantities, the bending energy and a component of the fluid impulse, into a functional that we prove is comparable to the squared $H^2$-distance from the corresponding orbit for all admissible curves. For circular arcs with angle $θ>π$, we prove nonlinear orbital instability using the inverse generalized Hasimoto transformation.

title: Examples of absolutely minimal polyhedral chains in maximum norm spaces
abstract: We construct explicit area-minimizing polyhedral disks in $\R^n$ with the maximum norm for $n=2,3,4$. Their boundaries are polygonal images of the geodesic circle of length $2π$, obtained from $n$ distance functions. Piecewise constant calibrations show that these disks minimize mass among Ambrosio--Kirchheim metric currents with the same boundary. The example for $n=4$ gives the lower bound $11π^2/20\approx5.42828$ for Gromov's filling area conjecture. For $n>4$, finite linear programs provide further lower bounds.

title: Sequential Entropic Optimal Transport for Bayesian Inverse Problems via Multilevel Monte Carlo
abstract: We consider the problem of Bayesian estimation associated to inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). In most cases of practical interest, one must use numerical solvers to implement computational methods based on Monte Carlo methods. This inevitably leads to an adaptation of multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) methods to reduce computational efforts to achieve a pre-specified mean square error (MSE). MLMC is based on sampling coupled versions of Bayesian posteriors associated to increasingly precise numerical solves of the PDE. In this article we present a novel method to implement MLMC based upon sequential entropic optimal transport couplings learned with light Schrödinger bridges, and correct the transport with Metropolis--Hastings steps that preserve the pairing. We bound the mean square error associated to a version of our new estimation method and show, for an elliptic inverse problem, that to achieve a MSE of $\mathcal{O}(δ^2)$ ($δ>0$) one can have an optimal cost of $\mathcal{O}(δ^{-2})$. The results feature explicit bounds on the effect of the fitted transport and of the Metropolis--Hastings correction. From a numerical perspective, on elliptic, Darcy-flow and Navier-Stokes problems, the method reduces the variance of the most precise solver by a factor of five to ten and is faster than multilevel sequential Monte Carlo [arXiv:1503.07259] at tight accuracies.

title: Broadcasting in Centimeter-Wave Gigantic MIMO Systems: Beam Shaping is All You Need
abstract: Beamforming is a key enabling technology for centimeter-wave Gigantic MIMO (G-MIMO) systems, using antenna arrays to generate wide beams for cell-wide broadcasting or narrow beams for data transmission. This paper presents a novel \emph{beam shaping technology} for designing environment-aware broadcast beams (i.e., beams for common control information delivery, as in 5G SSB). As a case study, we shape a \emph{prostrate beam} in the vertical plane to approximate uniform electromagnetic power distribution across the ground, thereby enhancing broadcast coverage quality. We first propose a geometric broadcasting model that, through coordinate transformation, relates base station height, beam spread, maximum service distance, and downtilt angle. Building on this model and the signal propagation model, we formulate the beam shaping problem as a non-convex optimization problem that aims to maximize ground-level coverage. To solve it, we develop a generalized optimization framework. We reformulate the problem into a matrix representation, equivalently transforming it into a target pursuit optimization (TPO) problem. Using variable substitution, the objective is convexified into a quadratically constrained quadratic program, and the non-convex rank constraint is handled via successive convex approximation, decomposing the problem into iteratively solved subproblems. We provide complexity and convergence analyses for the proposed algorithm. Numerical simulations confirm that the optimization effectively shapes the intended beam pattern and that the proposed prostrate beam yields significant performance gains, including substantially extended coverage distance, over conventional wide-beam benchmarks.

title: The minimal period solution of Hamiltonian systems with even potentials
abstract: We consider the autonomous system $\ddot{q}+\nabla V(q)=0$ in an arbitrary finite-dimensional Euclidean space. The potential is assumed to be even, nonnegative and of class $C^2$, to satisfy $V(x)=o(|x|^2)$ at the origin, and the Ambrosetti--Rabinowitz superquadratic inequality outside a ball. We prove that, for every prescribed $T>0$, the system has a nonconstant solution with $T$ being its minimal positive period.

title: Symmetry Inheritance and Exact Mirror Symmetry Reduction for Electric Field Vector Wave Problems with PEC Boundaries
abstract: A symmetry-inheritance and exact domain-reduction framework is developed for the second-order vector wave equation of the electric field in bounded domains with a perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary and general spatially varying anisotropic media. Orthogonal group actions on polar vectors, axial vectors, and second-order constitutive tensors are used to derive the transformed curl--curl equation and PEC trace directly from the original boundary-value problem. Under unique solvability, the common symmetry group of the problem data is inherited by the electric field. When the symmetry group of the electromagnetic medium admits a mirror symmetry, an arbitrary impressed current can be decomposed by the associated reflection projectors into mirror-even and mirror-odd components. The corresponding full-domain fields inherit the respective parities, and their exact restriction to one half-domain yields a perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) condition for the even field and a PEC condition for the odd field. The original problem is therefore represented exactly by two independent reduced-domain problems. A symmetry-compatible first-family Nédélec discretization preserves this decomposition at the discrete level. Analytical and numerical results verify the symmetry-inheritance theory, the exact PEC/PMC reduced-domain formulations, and the discrete reconstruction for constant and spatially varying anisotropic conductive media under both symmetric and asymmetric excitations.

title: Exploiting Pinching Antenna Systems in NOMA Covert Communication Networks
abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) provide flexible transmitter-side radiation reconfiguration for high-frequency wireless communications. This paper applies PASS to non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) covert communication networks, where activated pinching antennas (PAs) transmit superimposed signals to a pair of users stochastically distributed within a rectangle. Two passive wardens respectively monitor the downlink transmissions intended for two users. More specifically, we derive the closed-form detection error probability (DEP) expressions for two wardens under bounded noise uncertainty. Then we analytically determine the optimal detection thresholds and minimum DEPs in the worst-case covert detection scenarios. The covert transmission rates of two users are further characterized by taking into consideration ideal successive interference cancellation and non-ideal successive interference cancellation at near user and intra-NOMA interference at far user. Numerical results are presented to confirm that: 1) PASS-NOMA is capable of providing higher covert rates relative to conventional orthogonal multiple access OMA schemes; 2) As the number of activated PAs begun to increase, the near user has ability to obtain a larger covert rate gain than far user; and 3) The DEP of PASS-NOMA networks is larger than that of both PASS-OMA and traditional antenna (TA) based NOMA in specific output power regions.

title: Adaptive Grid Refinement for Optimal Feedback Control
abstract: This paper introduces an algorithmic approach for adaptive grid refinement for solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) partial differential equation (PDE) to obtain the optimal feedback control. Traditional grid generation methods often face challenges associated with state-space dimensionality, solution regularity, and large variations in the solution. Whereas fixed grid generation methods may fail to capture the intricate details of the optimal solution, our methodology addresses this challenge by dynamically refining the grid used to solve the HJB equation, thereby optimizing computational resource usage while targeting improved solution accuracy. The reinforcement learning (RL)-based approach presented in this study seeks to reduce the node population while constructing a grid with higher node density in regions with large discretization error.

title: Tamed Euler Approximation of Invariant Measures for Weakly Interacting Particle Systems and McKean--Vlasov Equations
abstract: We analyze explicit tamed Euler approximations for weakly interacting particle systems and McKean--Vlasov diffusions with additive noise and polynomially weighted locally Hölder, possibly superlinear drift.Under dissipativity at infinity and suitable stability assumptions, we establish time-uniform $W_1$ bounds by reflection coupling, separating relaxation, time-discretization, and finite-particle errors.For small step sizes, we prove existence and uniqueness of numerical invariant laws and bound their error relative to the continuous-time particle invariant law uniformly in $N$ in a normalized joint $W_1$ distance. We further bound the error of the one-particle numerical invariant marginal relative to the McKean--Vlasov invariant law by $O(θ^{\min\{α,β/2\}}+N^{-1/2})$, where $θ$ is the step size, $N$ the particle number, $α\in(0,1/2]$ the taming exponent, and $β\in(0,1]$ the Hölder exponent. Analytical examples illustrate the framework for smooth and non-Lipschitz drifts.

title: Effective stability and sharp logarithmic time scales for Hamiltonian PDEs on the circle
abstract: We prove effective stability and matching logarithmic upper bounds for small solutions of Hamiltonian PDEs on the one-dimensional torus. An analytic coefficient-majorant calculus and an explicit normal-form iteration yield stability times with logarithms of order $L^{1+1/p}/(\log L)^{1/p}$ for Gevrey weights and $L^{1+(q-1)/(pq+1)}$ for logarithmic ultra-differentiable weights, where $L=\log(1/\varepsilon)$ and $p\geq1$ measures the order dependence of the small divisors. Even frequencies are organized into the exact blocks $\{n,-n\}$; elementary frequency gaps and constant weights on these blocks close the energy estimate. We verify the hypotheses for convolution NLS, fractional NLS with every fixed noninteger exponent $η>1/2$, and a beam equation with a metric parameter and a variational gradient nonlinearity. Two fixed analytic nonlocal Hamiltonian PDEs admit finite-support solutions whose first prescribed norm amplification occurs on the same logarithmic scales along sequences $\varepsilon_n\to0$. The common lower theorem applies to every sufficiently small datum of each admissible equation. Its combination with these examples establishes sharpness of both regularity-dependent scales under the same analytic and arithmetic hypotheses.

title: Counting and constructing Latin tableaux
abstract: Latin tableaux generalize Latin squares to Young diagrams and have interesting connections to linear algebra and Rota's basis conjecture. Conjecturally, a partition admits Latin tableaux if and only if it belongs to a special class called wide partitions. We prove that various classes of wide partitions admit Latin tableaux. We extend these classes further by showing that the number of Latin tableaux is weakly increasing over certain operations on wide partitions. Additionally, we establish an explicit formula for the number of Latin tableaux using (0,1)-matrices and matrix permanents.

title: Bistable Dynamics and Complete Classifications of A Seasonal Competition Model Between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus
abstract: The bistable dynamics and a complete classification of global dynamics are established for a competition model between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus subject to favorable-unfavorable seasonal shifts, originally proposed by Zheng et al. (2025). More precisely, by employing Floquet theory, we prove that the unique positive periodic solution must be unstable. Consequently, bistable dynamics naturally emerge, which provides a rigorous theoretical validation of the numerical simulation results reported in the aforementioned work. Building on this, we further derive a full classification of the model's global dynamics. In addition, we carry out a comprehensive analysis of how seasonal switching mechanisms govern the competitive outcomes between these two mosquito species, thereby offering insights into their ecological coexistence and potential displacement.

title: The Local Dyadic Conjecture
abstract: A rational with denominator a power of two is said to be dyadic. A long standing conjecture of Paul Seymour predicts that for an ideal clutter, the dual of the set covering problem always admits an optimal solution where all variables take dyadic values. We present a local version of this conjecture, and motivate it by proving an important special case.

title: Curvature-Scaled Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Convergence Beyond Smoothness
abstract: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) has established itself as a widely used method for training deep neural networks. Despite its popularity, existing convergence guarantees for SAM-type methods require smoothness, a restrictive assumption. Generalized smoothness conditions have recently been proposed in the analysis of gradient methods but remain underexplored for SAM. To analyze the effect of SAM's perturbation under generalized smoothness, we use relative gradient distortion to quantify how the sharpness-aware direction departs from the original gradient. Under $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness, we show that this distortion can become unbounded near stationarity for SAM and at large gradients for its unnormalized variant (USAM), with examples where SAM cycles and USAM diverges. We then establish a necessary condition for uniform distortion control among perturbations along the gradient whose nonnegative multipliers depend only on its norm. Motivated by this condition, we propose Curvature-Scaled SAM (CS-SAM), which scales both the perturbation and the descent step by suitable curvature upper bounds, and prove that it uniformly bounds the distortion. Under both $(L_0,L_1)$- and $(H_0,H_1)$-smoothness, we establish deterministic $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ rates for the best squared gradient norm on nonconvex objectives, last-iterate $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ rates for the function gap on convex objectives with a minimizer, and linear convergence under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition. With zero perturbation, our guarantees recover the rates for gradient descent with $(L_0,L_1)$- or $(H_0,H_1)$-based step-sizes. Minibatch experiments on computer vision tasks demonstrate competitive performance for both variants, with the $(H_0,H_1)$ variant achieving the highest mean best-test accuracy in all four settings against tuned SAM and USAM with constant and cosine annealing schedules.

title: ORSMT: Unleashing the Potential of Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Semantic Verification and Repair in LLM-Based Optimization
abstract: Large language models increasingly automate optimization modeling from natural language problems, producing written mathematics, solver code and a returned report. Verifying one optimization problem across these artifacts requires semantic comparison: unequal models can attain the same objective, equivalent models can use different auxiliary variables, and mutually consistent artifacts can omit the same source requirement. ORSMT provides a typed semantic interface and exact SMT relation queries. It aligns observable decisions, projects auxiliary variables, proves or refutes feasible region and objective relations, localizes refutations to implicated rows or domains and links source texts when available. It then reconstructs one artifact from another, and each adopted candidate passes the required relation checks.
